hook.text: A shirt that repels stains, kills bacteria, and blocks UV — all from invisible nanoparticle coatings on the fibers.

buildup.text: Nano-coated textiles use TiO₂ for UV protection, Ag for antimicrobial action, and silica for water repellency.

discovery.text: Nanoparticles bond to fiber surfaces via sol-gel or pad-dry-cure processes — surviving dozens of wash cycles.

twist.text: Each wash releases some nanoparticles into wastewater — the environmental cost of stain-proof clothing.

climax.text: Smart nano-textiles now sense body temperature and moisture — wearable health monitors woven into everyday clothes.

punchline.text: Invisible coatings turn ordinary fabric into high-tech gear you can wear.

quiz.question: What is a concern with nano-coated textiles?
options: They make clothes too heavy to wear
Nanoparticles shed during washing and enter wastewater
They change the color of fabrics permanently
